AfterModifyingCardRewardOptions.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 6): both halves. (1) THE FLAG EXISTS: rewards.py now carries `CardCreationFlags` (src/Core/Runs/CardCreationFlags.cs, the source's own values) on CardCreationOptions, and `IS_CARD_REWARD` is set exactly where C# sets it -- CardReward.cs:114-115 and :134, i.e. a card reward SCREEN and nothing else -- so SilkenTress.cs:53-56's `!options.Flags.HasFlag(CardCreationFlags.IsCardReward)` is now a real guard and a relic or event generation no longer burns the one-shot. (2) THE CHARGE MOVED TO ITS OWN HOOK: the two modifier passes now collect the listeners that returned TRUE (Hook.cs:1445-1467) and `after_modify_card_reward_options` notifies exactly those (Hook.cs:679-690, dispatched from CardFactory.cs:106 and CardReward.cs:153), which is where SilkenTress.cs:75-81 sets IsUsed. The sim's fused write inside the modifier is gone. Pinned by test_silken_tress_does_not_spend_itself_on_a_non_reward.  The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: C# spends the charge from a SEPARATE hook, and Hook.AfterModifyingCardRewardOptions only notifies models that RETURNED TRUE from the modifier pass (Hook.cs:679-690 walks the listeners and skips any not in the `modifiers` list collected at Hook.cs:1445-1467). So the charge is spent exactly when the relic declined to return false -- and SilkenTress.cs:47-73 returns false on three conditions: wrong owner, not a card reward, already used. The sim's fused write at silken_tress.py:35 is reached after only ONE of those three (the `is_used` check at line 30). The owner check is structurally satisfied (single-player), so the observable divergence is the IsCardReward clause: guard G1's executed evidence shows Lead Paperweight's pickup burning the one-shot. Correct in one respect worth pinning: C# returns true (and therefore spends the charge) even when the loop enchanted NOTHING -- the `return true` at SilkenTress.cs:72 is unconditional after the loop -- so the sim setting is_used unconditionally at line 35 is right, and a 'only spend it if something got enchanted' fix would be a NEW divergence. Rule 7: Hook.cs and rewards.py are not hashed here.

guards.issue: RECONFIRMED 2026-08-04 (stale-sweep): brain_leech.py has been rewritten again since round 6 (it now builds the RIP screen through `CardRewardGroup(...).populate()`, rewards.py:639-649, which passes `is_card_reward=True` at rewards.py:646, rather than the old bare `modify_hooks` flag this record's history describes) -- RE-EXECUTED against TODAY'S code, not the stale `relic_probes_b14.py card-reward-flag` probe (which still calls the OLD `create_reward_cards(modify_hooks=...)` shape directly and no longer represents brain_leech.py's real code path, so its case-(b)/(c) printouts are decoration, not evidence). Directly invoked the live BrainLeech methods against a run holding both Silver Crucible and Silken Tress: `ev._rip()` -> times_used 0->1, is_used False->True (matches C#'s 1/True); `ev._share_knowledge()` -> times_used 0, is_used False (matches C#'s clear-flag 0/False, since ForNonCombatWithDefaultOdds never sets IsCardReward); a bare `run.add_relic('lead_paperweight')` pickup (LeadPaperweight.cs:21-22's bare CreateForReward, IsCardReward clear) -> times_used 0, is_used False (matches C#). All three reproduce C# exactly. STILL CLOSED, and more robustly than before: (1) THE FLAG EXISTS: rewards.py now carries `CardCreationFlags` (src/Core/Runs/CardCreationFlags.cs, the source's own values) on CardCreationOptions, and `IS_CARD_REWARD` is set exactly where C# sets it -- CardReward.cs:114-115 and :134, i.e. a card reward SCREEN and nothing else -- so SilkenTress.cs:53-56's `!options.Flags.HasFlag(CardCreationFlags.IsCardReward)` is now a real guard and a relic or event generation no longer burns the one-shot. (2) THE CHARGE MOVED TO ITS OWN HOOK: the two modifier passes now collect the listeners that returned TRUE (Hook.cs:1445-1467) and `after_modify_card_reward_options` notifies exactly those (Hook.cs:679-690, dispatched from CardFactory.cs:106 and CardReward.cs:153), which is where SilkenTress.cs:75-81 sets IsUsed. The sim's fused write inside the modifier is gone. Pinned by test_silken_tress_does_not_spend_itself_on_a_non_reward.  The text it replaced read (HISTORICAL, no longer current code): MECHANISM: C# refuses to touch the options unless `options.Flags.HasFlag(CardCreationFlags.IsCardReward)`, and that flag is set by exactly two places in the whole game -- CardReward's two constructors (CardReward.cs:113-115 and :134) and the SealedDeck modifier (SealedDeck.cs:30). Every other CardFactory.CreateForReward caller leaves it clear, and CardFactory dispatches the hook regardless (CardFactory.cs:104, gated on the DIFFERENT flag NoModifyHooks), so this flag is the relic's own gate and nothing else enforces it. The sim has no flag at all: rewards.py:299-301 runs modify_card_reward_options for every create_reward_cards call whose `modify_hooks` argument is True -- and that argument is NoModifyHooks, not IsCardReward. Three ported call sites are therefore wrong, EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b14.py card-reward-flag): (a) relics/lead_paperweight.py:24-29 passes modify_hooks=True where LeadPaperweight.cs:21-22 builds a bare CardCreationOptions and calls CreateForReward directly -- IsCardReward CLEAR, so C# skips both relics; the probe offers [('restlessness', 1, 'glam'), ('impatience', 1, 'glam')] and reports Silver Crucible's times_used 0 -> 1 and Silken Tress's is_used False -> True, where C# offers two unmodified level-0 Colorless cards and spends neither relic. (b) events/brain_leech.py:44's SHARE_KNOWLEDGE leaves modify_hooks at its True default where BrainLeech.cs:66 is also a bare CreateForReward (ForNonCombatWithDefaultOdds) -- IsCardReward CLEAR; the probe reports six upgraded options and times_used 1. (c) the OPPOSITE direction: events/brain_leech.py:60's RIP passes modify_hooks=False, but BrainLeech.cs:57 builds a real `new CardReward(options, 3, Owner)` whose Populate sets IsCardReward -- so C# DOES modify those options and the sim does not; the probe reports three level-0 options and times_used 0. The reference case is correct on both sides: a normal combat card reward fires (probe case (d): three level-1 options, times_used 1). REACHABILITY (LIVE): both relics come from Neow's curse pool at floor 0 (events/neow.py:47); Lead Paperweight is in Neow's positive pool (events/neow.py:39) and Brain Leech is a ported event any run can roll (events/__init__.py:118) -- so a run holding either relic and reaching either site diverges, with no further content needed. The observable is compound: the wrong CARDS are offered, and a limited charge is spent (or not spent), which changes what the NEXT card reward looks like. The fix is a field, not a flag flip: create_reward_cards needs an is_card_reward parameter distinct from modify_hooks, and its four ported callers need auditing against their C# counterparts -- brain_leech's two arms are currently inverted. Rule 7: CardReward.cs, CardFactory.cs, SealedDeck.cs, LeadPaperweight.cs, BrainLeech.cs, rewards.py, relics/lead_paperweight.py, events/brain_leech.py and events/neow.py are not hashed here. AT THIS UNIT'S SITE specifically: Silken Tress is one-shot, so a wrongly-fired enchant does not merely add Glam to the wrong cards -- it permanently consumes the relic, and the player's NEXT card reward (the one the relic is for) comes out unenchanted.

guards.what: N1: `RunState.CloneCard(card)` then `cardReward.ModifyCard(card2, this)` (SilkenTress.cs:67-69) vs the sim enchanting the offered card in place (silken_tress.py:34) -- PROMPT.md class 17
guards.rationale: MECHANISM: C# does not mutate the offered card. It clones it (`base.Owner.RunState.CloneCard(card)`), edits the CLONE, and swaps it in through `cardReward.ModifyCard(card2, this)`, which keeps the untouched `originalCard` alongside it -- LastingCandy.cs:115's `o.originalCard.Id` is the one reader of that field in the game. The sim edits the offered Card object in place. PROMPT.md class 17 flags shallow rebuilds that DROP per-instance state, and this site is the inverse: because the sim mutates rather than rebuilds, enchantment, affliction and cost modifiers survive by construction, which is also what CloneCard's ClonePreservingMutability does (CardModel.cs:2168-2179). So the OFFERED card is equivalent on both sides and binding rule 2 is satisfied -- verdicted deliberate-divergence, not a gap. Two residues recorded rather than waved through: the sim cannot answer `originalCard` at all, which a ported Lasting Candy would need; and an unpicked C# clone is a real CardModel created on the run, so if RunState.CloneCard ever gains a side effect (a net-id counter, a discovered-cards ledger) the counts diverge. Neither is observable today. Rule 7: CardModel.cs, LastingCandy.cs and cards/base.py are not hashed here.

guards.rationale: The consequence, for the record: a conformance-runner relic swap cannot restore the lost gold, and unlike a max-HP relic there is no record of how much was taken -- so this unit would need the pre-loss balance captured to be undoable at all.
